120	This was actually the occasion on which the Rebbe conveyed to the shluchim the message that he had conveyed
121	more generally before to all of Israel, all the Chassidim, all of Israel.
122	And here the Rebbe says it in a much more explained way.
123	So indeed, what is new in this sichah, as we said earlier,
124	is that even what the Rebbe said in the sichah of 28 Nissan was still something very, very small, you could
125	call it a point.
126	It was still not something with a whole work plan.
127	On the contrary, those were words so powerful that they opened a great
128	many question marks.
129	Like, what does the Rebbe mean, and what does it say, and so too all sorts of things that...
130	they tried to do some of them, and the Rebbe also encouraged it greatly, but it wasn't clear that this alone is what the Rebbe
131	means.
132	And when this sichah comes, it is a sichah with exclamation marks, not question marks.
133	That is, it is very clear what the Rebbe wants from us in this work.
134	So that is one point: this sichah is a kind of closing of the circle of what
135	was opened on 28 Nissan, but there is another, no less significant point,
136	that this sichah is actually the detail, that is, there is the
137	general and the particular, right?
138	It is actually the particular of the general that was in the previous sichah.
139	In the previous sichah the Rebbe shared with us a most wondrous heavenly process, which began
140	on Shabbat Parashat Noach.
141	On Shabbat Parashat Noach the Rebbe made a cheshbon tzedek
142	with the Holy One, blessed be He, about the situation: what is happening?
143	Why has Moshiach still not come?
144	And then the conclusion was the conclusion of the cheshbon tzedek: since all the work has been completed,
145	and even though perhaps each one personally can notice that he has things that need correcting, the Rebbe said that this should
146	not confuse us into thinking that it affects the general situation or the general balance of the Jewish people.
147	Because on the contrary, the general situation is totally perfect, and the fact that each and every one has
148	private matters not only does not harm at all, but on the contrary, from the power of the whole one can
149	easily and quickly correct the private matters too. It is like a person who is healthy
150	in every sense; even if he has some small scratch on his finger, it does not change his state of health,
151	because it is a private matter that does not touch the whole.
152	So if the Jewish people here is not ready for the Redemption, then where is the Redemption?
153	So the Rebbe said that we reach the conclusion that it depends on nothing other than Moshiach Tzidkeinu himself.
154	That is, the entire matter must be focused on Moshiach.
155	What does that mean in practice?
156	So the Rebbe says that this, that it depends only on Moshiach Tzidkeinu himself, must find expression
157	in a special way in Kiddush Levanah.
158	For Kiddush Levanah is an opportunity to ask the Holy One, blessed be He, to reveal Moshiach to us, because this is what we say in Kiddush
159	Levanah: "They shall seek HaShem their God, and David their king." Amen.
160	In effect, the Rebbe turns to the Chassidim and says that there is an auspicious time here, to make use of
161	it and ask the Holy One, blessed be He, for the coming of Moshiach.
162	Now, we know many stories of an auspicious time throughout the generations, that there was an auspicious time for the Redemption,
163	and also with the Rebbe, that the auspicious time was not used.
164	It was an opportunity, an exit to the Redemption, and, God forbid, because of shortsightedness
165	they missed the matter.
166	One of the most famous stories is about the Arizal: on Erev Shabbat Kodesh he said to all his holy students, all of them
167	were supreme tzaddikim.
168	And he said to them, let us go to Jerusalem.
169	Let us go to the Redemption.
170	And they, as the saying goes, in a missed moment,
171	said, fine, we will just go notify the wife at home so that she won't wait for Kiddush,
172	right?
173	Then, all at once, the Arizal was very distressed and said that there was an auspicious time
174	that we lost.
175	Had they not asked, but gone immediately, the Redemption would have come.
176	And this is just a story that is an example of many such opportunities.
177	And here it is actually an opportunity in which the Rebbe, so to speak, revealed to us the auspicious time to ask for the Redemption
178	and to bring about the coming of Moshiach, and, thank HaShem, the Rebbe himself told
179	us afterward that it was accepted, that this auspicious time achieved its effect.
180	What was the continuation?
181	The continuation was that the Kiddush Levanah was actually held not on Motzaei Shabbat of Noach, because that was too early,
182	but on Motzaei Shabbat of Parashat Lech Lecha, a week later,
183	and therefore in the sichah of Parashat Lech Lecha, which was before Motzaei Shabbat, one does not yet see a clear continuation
184	of this matter, but in the sichah of Parashat Vayera, which is actually the first farbrengen of
185	the Rebbe after the Kiddush Levanah, the Rebbe says in the most explicit way
186	that since they asked "HaShem their God" in Kiddush Levanah, the request was accepted by the Holy One, blessed be He,
187	and it was fixed, so the reality, not only does the reality of Moshiach exist, but also the revelation of
188	Moshiach.
189	That is, the Rebbe really shares with us this heavenly knowledge, that this request
190	indeed achieved its effect, and the Holy One, blessed be He, on His part, already gives us
191	not only the...
192	not only gives Moshiach to be found among us, but actually gives him the...
193	okay, so to speak, the permission to be revealed.
194	And so already in this sichah of Parashat Vayera, the previous sichah, the Rebbe said: so what
195	is the work now?
196	So what should we focus on now?
197	So from there the clear matter begins, that the work now is to receive Moshiach Tzidkeinu, which is the thing that remains.
198	When we say "the only thing that remains," it does not mean that we must stop everything we did until today, but rather it is
199	the only thing that remains in the sense that everything we did until today and continue to do
200	must be focused and directed toward this matter of receiving Moshiach.
201	But still, no one understands exactly how to do this.
202	Especially since the example the Rebbe brought there in the sichah of Parashat Vayera was a very, very
203	wondrous example.
204	The Rebbe said that a Jew must reach a state in which even during eating he so longs to eat the
205	feast of the Leviathan and the Shor HaBar,
206	that he is unable to be satisfied from the eating; he remains hungry
207	for the feast of the Leviathan and the Shor HaBar, even though he ate to satiety
208	and ate as he was accustomed to eat until today.
209	But in human nature, when a person eats and is not focused on what he is eating, he thinks of another menu he would like
210	to eat, and not just wants, but truly longs, then he is not able to be truly satisfied from what he
211	eats.
212	To such a degree that he comes to the Holy One, blessed be He, with a complaint and says: You...
213	commanded in the Torah "and you shall eat and be satisfied and bless," and You do not give me the opportunity to fulfill this mitzvah as
214	it should be, to be satisfied and to bless.
215	So we understand that there is here truly a very, very high demand, of
216	how much a Jew must be permeated with anticipation and longing
217	for the revelation of Moshiach with all that this implies, including the feast of the Leviathan and the Shor HaBar, and at a level
218	so tangible that he is unable to be satisfied from what he eats.
219	But still this does not necessarily give us a clear, ordered teaching
220	of how to implement this matter step by step, each one according to his level,
221	and in all the details of the service of HaShem.
222	So here, afterward, when the shluchim arrive, as I said earlier, beyond the closing of the circle of
223	that mission, in relation to the mission of Pesach Nitzan, there is also a clear continuation.
224	In the previous sichah, the Rebbe opens the sichah immediately, and since he finished the previous sichah, now he finished
225	the matter that all the work now is to receive Moshiach Tzidkeinu, and here the Rebbe opens the sichah.
226	And so, if this is the work of the shluchim, then the shluchim's role and task is to influence all
227	of the Jewish people, each and every one in his place, so this is actually the new order of work of the Jewish people in
228	our generation: receiving Moshiach Tzidkeinu.
229	And this matter the Rebbe now begins to expand on and explain, as we said earlier, both on levels of depth
230	of understanding and on practical levels of work, bringing
231	this down to the practical level.
232	So he says as follows: it was also spoken of several times.
233	We will dwell on the common point in the general work of shlichut of the Jewish people in general, that they are the emissaries of the Holy One,
234	blessed be He.
235	And what is the most general work of shlichut of the Jewish people in all generations?
236	It is, in the language of the Sages, "I was created to serve my Maker."
237	The Holy One, blessed be He, descends from the upper worlds into the physical body here in this world,
238	as a kind of mission.
239	And in this sense every Jew is a shaliach by his very being, and what is his mission?
